   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Brian Birkett, CO. DURHAM.

Dear Ron and Brian,


I was saddened at the threaten-
ing situation which confronts
you all. I can only add my
gratitude for your devotion and
wish you better times ahead.


I visited the ALL FORMAT'S SHOW
at Washington, Tyne & Wear and I
am pleased to say that the turn
out from both public and exibit-
ors was a great improvement from
the last one which was dismal to
say the least. A lot of work
must have been put in by the
organsisers to improve things.

The Spectrum and SAM lacked sup-
port whilst other formats found
favour, I had to look hard for
any Spectrum items. What did
strike me was the interest in a
bias towards music generation!

Whilst I was awaiting entry, I
noticed that almost everyone had
a `1 off voucher,and thought why
don't the organisers drop the
price and save the trouble of
producing vouchers.There must be
some advertising value in these
vouchers as they are not diffic-
ult to get hold of, and it must
cost something to produce them
in their differing formats.

After reading a letter from
Stephen Baines (OUTLET 65) re:


adding a second 3.5" drive. I
decided to have a bash. Since
GREENWELD are out of FD9s,I pur-
chased an uncased Citizen unit
from the All Formats Show and
have proved it works by temp.
substituting my Lifetime drive.
(Both units look identical).

When it came to thinking of a
more permanent solution, looking
for the regulated 5 volt supply
inside the case of my black +2
(1988 iss.2 board), I found that
the terminals were marked GND,
PLAY, +5,and REC. The fifth pin
nearest the front of the key-
board is unwired. Am I correct
in assuming that the the GND and
+5 pins are to be used, also can
the cassette be left connected?


I occasionally use a Panasonic
KX-P1124 24 pin printer that can
emulate Epson LQ-2500 and find
that using the TABLOID function
text spills over the page length
giving approx. 1 full page plus
14 lines followed by a formfeed.
This wastes well over 3/4 of a
page as the printing starts
again at the top of the third
sheet. Is this is under software
control?


Although I can change the Form
Length at the printer this makes
no difference to the output.I've
also tried making a new system
disk but the parameters in the
printer manual don't allow for
exact entry to prompts given.


Is there anything I can change
to get a normal output and perf-
oration skip over using 11.5"
fanfold paper?

On another theme, going back a
while, when I tried to LOAD the
ROM INDEX (+D 3.5" version) from
Issue 51, I found file C2 failed
to load giving "End of File"
error, so if you can find time,
could you please put it on this
disk when returned.


        Yours sincerely,

         Brian Birkett

Brian Cavers to Brian Birkett

Some years ago I bought a ream
of 11.5" printer paper and found
it to be nothing but trouble! I
swore never again! 11" is the
standard A4 printer paper while
11.5" is the "true" A4.

I only have ordinary 11" paper
here now so I have tried to
simulate 11.5" paper by ruling a
pencil line every 11.5" and
setting my printer's page length
to 11.5". The print out is fine
using TABLOID and this is as to
be expected because the routine
simply prints a page of text and
then sends a form feed. So long
as the page is not too SHORT it
should work on any page length.

You might try the following but
I don't think it will help to be
honest!...

BREAK into the BASIC and edit
line 1610. This is a large line
so it may be better to do it in
48K mode. Insert the following
into the first LPRINT statement
AFTER the E$;"@"; but BEFORE the
next E$...
            E$;"CE";

so the line starts roughly...

1610 LPRINT E$;"@";E$;"CE";E$...

Now enter RUN and try it. If it
fails try selecting the CUTSHEET
option and wind the paper
manually when it pauses at the
end of printing each sheet.

Failing all that, check that you
have no other unusual switches
set on your printer.

Finally, please send me a print
out of what you get including at
least three sheets so I can see
end and start as well as any
progression. You see the problem
is that it is not totally clear
from your description. Are the
"14 lines"you get blank or text?
Is the full page you mention a
TABLOID page of 12 screen pages
or do you mean the physical page
(sheet)? Does the text actually
print over the perforation? In
my test I got 14 blank lines at
the end of TABLOID page which
took it correctly to the start
of the next sheet.

It is possible your printer is
not entirely Epson-compatible
despite what Panasonic claim.
Does it accept ESC "O" (CHR$ 79)
to clear the skip perforation
auto-formfeed for example?

On reflection, I wonder if your
printer forces a formfeed? The
other possibility is that your
printer will not accept the line
spacing code which may make the
text size and line spaces a bit
higher thus overruning the sheet
onto the next sheet for a few
lines and then TABLOID sends its
FORMFEED. That linespacing is in
the TABLOID code so I will have
to hack into it but it still may
not be possible. Anyway, I'll
wait till I see your printout.

I didn't send you the faulty"c2"
file because I thought it was in
one of the succeeding issues but
when I checked it was "c6" that
had been omitted! Therefore I am
now adding it to the ADD-ENDERS
in this issue (+D only) for you.

Incidentally, it was O.K. on the
original 51 master so it may be
you have resaved some other file
on your copy of the disc and the
G+DOS sometimes corrupts discs
in this way. I urge people using
G+DOS NOT to resave files onto
their OUTLET discs and take care
with other discs!I RECOMMEND ALL
OF YOU +D USERS TO BUY BETADOS
(reviewed in this issue) AS IT
CURES THIS PROBLEM (as well as
having other extra features!)
                         - Brian

From Malcom Perry,KIDDERMINSTER



Dear Ron and Brian

HELP !!! How can I get SAM CODE
files into my Disciple? Normal
LOAD or Px fail with "invalid
file name".

It is so I can use my SAM assem-
bler for Spectrum MC routines.
My clumsy and long-winded method
so far has been to find out
which sector the file is on,load
into Disciple at sector level
and then resave as normal CODE
file (remembering to remove the
header and tail bits of code the
normal DOS adds on).

Is there a method without having
to alter the directory info and
first 9 bytes of the file to
form Disciple accepts?

         Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

SAMTOD in OUTLET 46 converts SAM
code files to +D format. I seem
to remember a slight bug with
files over 16384 in length but I
cured that later as I use SAMTOD
quite a lot myself (any problem
let me know).

If you have the COMET assembler,
I have put a copy of my COMET
(BASIC ONLY!!!) on your disc and
this saves the object code as ZX
code! You can't use it without
the COMET code and if you have
not got that then get it now -it
is the best! Alternatively, you
may be able to adapt the routine
to the assembler you use.I can't
put this SAM BASIC in ADDENDERS
as it won't copy.

In addition, I have modified my
own version of Tasword 2 to load
SAM text files directly and I
have extracted this routine from
my BASIC and put it in ADDENDERS
BUT NOTE: my Tasword 2 has been
totally rewritten so the lines
may need renumbering. They are
1700 to 1750 and you will need
to add a GO SUB somewhere. What
I did was to add a test to the
filename input:IF (string)begins
with "!" THEN GO SUB 1700.

Note that I cannot guarantee no
problems with the ordinary Tas2
BASIC. For instance, I used the
variable D for the current drive
(which I added at 1699 so you
can see).
                        - Brian

From: Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH

Dear Brian,

I saw your reply to George
Munro, and have just written a
short routine for PEEKing into
the +D's RAM. It's only 11 bytes
long. First the address is
RANDOMIZEd, then the following
routine is called:-


IN A, (231);     Page in +D
LD HL, (23670);  Get address
from "SEED"
LD C,(HL);       Put byte in BC
LD B,0;
OUT (231),A;     Page out +D
RET;             Back to BASIC



This routine could be used to
solve George Munro's problem of
detecting the current drive.
[Using RANDIMIZE 7642: PRINT USR
(code address)]

In your reply to Francis Miles'
letter you were wondering how to
ascertain whether a Disciple or
+D is connected. One way of
doing this would be to exploit
the fact that +D and Disciple
use a different offset for POKE
@. The following would do the
trick, using the last address in
the display file for the test:

10 POKE 22527,0
20 POKE @22527-8192,255
30 IF PEEK 22527=255...then +D,
otherwise Disciple.


Now, a couple of POKEs which
G+DOS users might find handy. I
saw them mentioned originally in
Format magazine, and they are
for allowing you to re-boot the
system file using RUN when the
DOS is still intact. These are
POKE @7652,0 and POKE @6000,10.
Both allow you to re-boot, but
there is an important difference
between them. POKE @7652,0
resets the +D RAM at the same
time, whereas POKE @6000,10 does
not corrupt the DOS and is
therefore very useful to include
in an AUTOLOAD file, e.g.
Catloader. (Betados, by the way,
has this facility built in).

Finally, a hardware tip for that
annoying 'sticking keys' problem


on the grey +2 (Caps M & N,
Symb. Shift/A, and in some cases
other keys too, depending on the
value the I register holds). I
read in Format of a permanent
cure for that problem, i.e. to
connect a 1000 pf capacitor
across Diode 35. Although this
fixes the problem in the 48K
Editor, it does not have any
effect on certain programs which
use interrupts and load the I
register with values other than
0 or 63. Tasword was especially
troublesome, as Symbol Shift/A
wouldn't work.

The cause of the problem was
said to be internal capacitance
of the keyboard not being opti-
mum,and this drifts as the


machine warms up, affecting the
timing of signals. This would
certainly explain the thermal
nature of the problem, which
completely baffled me for a long
time.

I had a look inside my Spectrum
and saw that Diode 35 was in
fact one of a series of 8 which
connect to the keyboard, and  I
wondered if connecting a capac-
itor across each of them (i.e.
D28 to D35)might improve things.
To my great delight I found that
it did, and experimenting with
different values showed that
whilst their exact values are
not critical, ones around 200 pf
or so worked fine. Too high
values (in excess of 1000 pf)


caused crashes with certain key
combinations, and ones less than
100 pf or so were too small to
be effective.

The result for me is a complete
cure - no trace of the effect
now in any circumstances, and no
need to patch programs any more
to get round it!

Well, that's about it for now.
Hope you manage to cope with the
money situation, and long may
OUTLET continue.

            Regards,

         Miles Kinloch

Brian Cavers to Miles Kinloch

I am currently working on a new
version of the PEEK @ program we
had previously in OUTLET that
will work on both Disciple and
the +D.I had also arrived at the
same idea as you to detect which
interface was connected although
I think 23565 is a better POKE
because 22527 corrupts the
screen and you cannot guarantee
that won't be a problem or at
least a nuisance in some program
or other!23565 is an interesting
"spare" system variable address
one can use to pass bytes as it
is only used temporarily to hold
the colour number when editing
colour codes directly so it can
only be 0 to 7 normally and POKE
does no harm.         - Brian

From: G.C. Wells, THETFORD

Dear Ron, Brian and All,

I've got to thank you lot for
all your help, the OUTLETs, and,
well, for just being a part of
the Speccy mob. In fact, without
you I don't think we would surv-
ive and the richer bods would
have moved onto higher ground.

To be honest, without what I've
got here and using; Oh yea! it's
the +3, V, 120D+ Citizen, and up
until now a Binatone B & W TV. I
never knew what I was missing as
I used to have to keep twiddling
the knobs to keep the blinking
screen from doing wonderful
imitations of a belly dancer.

Well, I went along to Thetford
Micros, spoke to one of the
people there and he said he had
a good second-hand monitor for
sale. So, I rallied around the
family, and got them to chip in
by bribing them to play Bingo
from an OUTLET program. Behold!
I was able to pay for the
Monitor, a Fidelity CM14 Colour.

What I really want to get at is
that the chap brought it home to
me, plugged it in, and ugh! -
nothing. Then he took it back to
the shop with the Speccy, tel-
ling me he had adjusted it with
a +2 model as well. He brought
it back in the evening and now I
have as good a picture as I have
seen on the expensive computers.

(Now, here it comes!) Is there
anyone that can transfer a PYSON
BACKGAMMON program from tape to
+3 disk? I have tried, but you
know me. If it's possible, then
I am willing to pay.


Also, I saw a game called (I
think - Coo! What!) no, it was
painless, VALHALLA.  Is it
possible to get a copy to keep
me amused?  I am really not one
for games, but there you go! I
have never had a computer game,
except on OUTLET, of course,
and at 79, I thought it about
time I gave it a bash. Any
offers?.

Brian Cavers to George Wells


Interesting list of hardware you
have George but I couldn't help
wondering what a "V" was! Also,I
preferred the belly dancer. The
PYSON BACKGAMMON I reckon is
meant to be "PSION", yes? Why
not save up for a Multiface 3?
It is the easiest way to get +3
programs on disc. Has anyone got
a copy of VALHALLA to sell?

I know there are OUTLET readers
who are ham radio enthusiasts
who could put you on the right
track for instance, Jim Hossack
and Andy Moir in this issue's
OUTLETTERS!

                      - Brian

From: A.C.Moir, 27 Cobham Close,
      Yapton, ARUNDEL, W.Sussex
      BN18 0L.  Tel:0243 552753

Dear All at OUTLET,

May I take this opportunity to
say a big thank you for the
great magazine that you produce
without failure every month. I
have a couple of enquiries.

1) Is there any way of stopping,
by a POKE statement, question
marks appearing either at the
beginning or end when printing?
I believe my printer is Epson
compatible as I don't have to
alter printer controls on
Tasword 2. My printer is a Micro
P CPA 80 - made in Japan.


2) Are there any OUTLETEERS out
there interested, like me, in
amateur radio? If so, it would
be nice to swap ideas etc.

Did you know there are probably
more programs for the Spectrum
for decoding data i.e.
C.W.(MORSE;RTTY;SSTV;AMTOR & FAX
than for any of the bigger
P.C.s, so anybody that says to
me - "huh, the Spectrum is just
a games machine" - gets a  right
lecture.

Anyway, again, many thanks to
you, and may I take this oppor-
tunity to say "Hi" to Mark
Payne, Arnold Yates, Les Tyler,
and Malcolm Perry - all who have
been such good friends over the
past few months.     - Andy Moir

Brian Cavers to Andy Moir

The question marks are line feed
codes(CHR$ 10). The Disciple and
+D print in two modes: one is
mainly intended for LLISTING
BASIC programs and this mode is
"switched on"by using POKE @6,0.
In this mode, printer codes such
as italics cannot be sent and a
question mark is sent instead!

You need to use POKE @ 6,1 and
then you can send printer codes.
If you enter in your Tasword 2
BASIC...

205 POKE @6,1
               ...and resave the
program at the menu then it will
be O.K.                - Brian

From: J. Hossack, WEST KILBRIDE

Dear Ron and Brian,

I have the Tasword +3 W.P. prog-
ram which has never given satis-
factory results on my Spectrum
+3. Most times it LOADs OK but
then it seems to go haywire,
particularly when I try to use
the "SAVE" option. I didn't
worry too much as I also have
Tasword 2, which works perfect-
ly; also it DID work OK some-
times, so I assumed my machine
might be to blame.

However, I read the letter from
Bill Clark (OUTLET 64). In your
reply you mention two different
versions of Tasword +3.


I was unaware that more than one
version existed, so wonder if I
have the wrong one for my mach-
ine. I enclose a copy of my ver-
sion and wonder if you would
check it (as you did with Mr.
Clark's) to see if it is unsuit-
able, leading to my problems.

I am having difficulty in locat-
ing the part of memory which
holds Tasword +3 text files.
(Tasword 2 are easy to find).
When I try to catalogue these
files I get a very low memory
location which is obviously
wrong. When I try to LOAD a file
from disc, using LOAD (file)
CODE I get the message "wrong
file type", and ditto if I try
to LOAD it as a DATA block.


If I could find the memory loc-
ation I could transfer the file
to Tasword 2 and so avoid the
problems of poor operation with
Tasword +3. I seem to remember
that you once published a prog-
ram to transfer text files from
Tasword 2 to Tasword +3, and I
wonder if there is a similar
program to do this in reverse?

To change tack: In OUTLET 65 you
give a listing program for radio
Q-codes. Would you be interested
in others of this type as I have
a number of such programs on
hand, including data-bases for
ham radio? If so, let me know.

By the way, I don't know if you
still pay for programs?I noticed


a suggestion that this might
help to avoid increased sub-
scriptions. If so I'd like to
register my support for the idea
- the satisfaction of having a
program accepted is usually
enough reward in itself without
payment! Best wishes to both -
and to OUTLET - for 1993!

I hope having my letter in the
32-character format as above
helps your editing procedure. By
the way, I've copied all the
files which refer to Tasword +3
on to disk, but NOT extras such
as Tasspell. I've also copied my
Tasword 2 (version from tape) so
you can LOAD these textfiles.
Also enclosed is your reply to
Mr. Clark as a printout, and a
short covering note. - J.Hossack

Brian Cavers to Jim Hossack

My version of Tasword +3 is the
same as yours and I could find
no problem loading. If there is
a particular text file that does
this then why not send it in so
I can try loading it on mine?
Does the same text file produce
the same error repeatedly? What
exactly is the error?

Possibly the text files are put
into 128K paged memory. Although
they may be shown in extended
CAT programs such as EXTENDACAT
(OUTLET 37) as CODE files, they
are actually special files. I'm
putting a program that converts
Tasword +3 files to Tasword 2 in
ADD-ENDERS if that helps.

By the way,I've noticed a lot of
users still use Tasword +3 with
the loading filename of "RUN". I
think this was probably set up
by Tasman before +3 dos was
finalised or published! It is
much easier to change the name
to "DISK" so you can boot it in!

Your text file was in 32 columns
but it should have been on the
left(from column 1 to column 32)
not in the centre.

I can't comment on a program
without seeing it. It is always
best to send it in and then I
can decide.We rarely reject any-
thing because of its type anyway
but only if it is copyright or
too large or badly bugged!-Brian

From: Brian Gaff, CHESSINGTON

The first point is not computer
related. I refer to this darned
cheque problem.I get a fair num-
ber of cheques and some are made
out to me personally,rather than
my business. In the old days, I
could sign them on the back and
pay them in.Not any more,as it's
not allowed! I do not know if
Format have this problem but
suspect they get them made out
to INDUG quite a lot, and there
is no way they can cash them!

Sector errors under UniDOS. I am
not sure but think these errors
are only in the way checksums
are calculated in the two DOSs.
I assume the so-called faulty

sectors appear to be OK when us-
ing BetaDOS? This was my exper-
ience,anyway.I too dumped UniDos
despite its many useful feat-
ures. You also have to watch the
use of the extra directory ent-
ries featured in BetaDos when
you may still have discs with
G-Dos on them. Life can get
tedious...

The problem drive could be a
couple of things. If it's a
Mitsubishi unit the chances are
that the head is below track 0.
This is a problem I had with
mine and it required a re-align-
ment of the track 0 sensor. On
the other hand, it could just be
jammed. Have a look,and turn the
stepper spindle so the head is


somewhere in the middle rather
than at one end. Now try it
again, if it works, a TINY bit
of sewing machine oil on the end
of the spindle can work wonders.

The PC Spectrum Emulator:I don't
think it entirely correct that I
review a product in which I have
a financial interest. I know
several OUTLET readers have the
current version, perhaps one of
them could review it!
      [IN THIS ISSUE! - BC]

Most people shy away from tract-
or feed labels because they get
stuck in the works. What I do is
get labels on a roll then sus-
pend this behind the printer on
a dowel pushed through a card-
board box of suitable height.

This seems to stop the snagging
as there is much less stress on
the tractor holes.

Disc drives. Though most current
Citizen drives - the ones descr-
ibed in last month's OUTLETTERS
- only need the 5V supply. There
are many drives that need 12V as
well, so be sure you know what
you're buying.In fact the double
supply system is the standard.

About a month BEFORE Samco was
wound up, I had been informed
that the SCPDSA was being wound
up.I assumed all those who need-
ed to know had been told.I think
it was really due to Brent hav-
ing to study more! I only live a
short distance from him, by the
way.

Poor Malcolm seems to get all
the bad luck!

The Greenweld PSU story goes
like this. There was a company
in Wales building PSUs for
SAMCo. They had done more than
they had been paid for. However,
they themselves failed about a
Month after SAMCo.All those PSUs
were sold at auction, though the
parts officially belonged to
SAMCo, not the other company.
Greenweld bought them, but had
no way to test them, and as a

Dear Brian,

I saw your reply to George Munro, and have just written a short routine for PEEKing into the +D's RAM. It's only 11 bytes long. First the address is RANDOMIZEd, then the following routine is called:-

IN A, (231);     Page in +D LD HL, (23670);  Get address from "SEED" LD C,(HL);       Put byte in BC LD B,0; OUT (231),A;     Page out +D RET;             Back to BASIC

This routine could be used to solve George Munro's problem of detecting the current drive. [Using RANDIMIZE 7642: PRINT USR (code address)]

In your reply to Francis Miles' letter you were wondering how to ascertain whether a Disciple or +D is connected. One way of doing this would be to exploit the fact that +D and Disciple use a different offset for POKE @. The following would do the trick, using the last address in the display file for the test:

10 POKE 22527,0 20 POKE @22527-8192,255 30 IF PEEK 22527=255...then +D, otherwise Disciple.

Now, a couple of POKEs which G+DOS users might find handy. I saw them mentioned originally in Format magazine, and they are for allowing you to re-boot the system file using RUN when the DOS is still intact. These are POKE @7652,0 and POKE @6000,10. Both allow you to re-boot, but there is an important difference between them. POKE @7652,0 resets the +D RAM at the same time, whereas POKE @6000,10 does not corrupt the DOS and is therefore very useful to include in an AUTOLOAD file, e.g. Catloader. (Betados, by the way, has this facility built in).

Finally, a hardware tip for that annoying 'sticking keys' problem

on the grey +2 (Caps M & N, Symb. Shift/A, and in some cases other keys too, depending on the value the I register holds). I read in Format of a permanent cure for that problem, i.e. to connect a 1000 pf capacitor across Diode 35. Although this fixes the problem in the 48K Editor, it does not have any effect on certain programs which use interrupts and load the I register with values other than 0 or 63. Tasword was especially troublesome, as Symbol Shift/A wouldn't work.

The cause of the problem was said to be internal capacitance of the keyboard not being opti- mum,and this drifts as the

machine warms up, affecting the timing of signals. This would certainly explain the thermal nature of the problem, which completely baffled me for a long time.

I had a look inside my Spectrum and saw that Diode 35 was in fact one of a series of 8 which connect to the keyboard, and  I wondered if connecting a capac- itor across each of them (i.e. D28 to D35)might improve things. To my great delight I found that it did, and experimenting with different values showed that whilst their exact values are not critical, ones around 200 pf or so worked fine. Too high values (in excess of 1000 pf)

caused crashes with certain key combinations, and ones less than 100 pf or so were too small to be effective.

The result for me is a complete cure - no trace of the effect now in any circumstances, and no need to patch programs any more to get round it!

Well, that's about it for now. Hope you manage to cope with the money situation, and long may OUTLET continue.

Regards,

Miles Kinloch

### От: Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH

Я прочел ваш ответ George Munro и только что написал короткую подпрограмму для PEEK в ОЗУ +D. Ее длина всего 11 байт. Сначала адрес задается через RANDOMIZE, а затем вызывается следующий код:

```text
IN A, (231);     Подключить ПЗУ/ОЗУ +D
LD HL, (23670);  Взять адрес из "SEED"
LD C,(HL);       Поместить байт в BC
LD B,0;
OUT (231),A;     Отключить +D
RET;             Назад в BASIC
```

Эту процедуру можно использовать для решения проблемы George Munro с определением текущего дисковода. [Используя `RANDOMIZE 7642: PRINT USR (адрес кода)`].

В ответе на письмо Francis Miles вы размышляли, как определить, подключен ли Disciple или +D. Один из способов — воспользоваться тем, что +D и Disciple используют разное смещение для команды POKE @. Для проверки подойдет следующий вариант с использованием последнего адреса экрана:

```basic
10 POKE 22527,0
20 POKE @22527-8192,255
30 IF PEEK 22527=255...тогда +D, иначе Disciple.
```

А теперь пара POKE, которые могут пригодиться пользователям G+DOS. Впервые я увидел их в журнале Format; они позволяют перезагрузить системный файл командой RUN, когда DOS еще находится в памяти. Это POKE @7652,0 и POKE @6000,10. Обе команды позволяют перезагрузиться, но между ними есть важное отличие: POKE @7652,0 одновременно сбрасывает ОЗУ +D, тогда как POKE @6000,10 не повреждает DOS и поэтому очень удобна для включения в файл AUTOLOAD, например, Catloader. (В Betados, кстати, эта функция встроена).

Наконец, аппаратный совет по поводу раздражающей проблемы с «залипанием клавиш» на сером +2 (Caps M и N, Symb. Shift/A, а в некоторых случаях и других клавиш, в зависимости от значения регистра I). В Format я вычитал способ окончательно решить эту проблему: подключить конденсатор емкостью 1000 пФ параллельно диоду 35 (Diode 35). Хотя это устраняет сбой в редакторе 48K, это не помогает в некоторых программах, которые используют прерывания и загружают в регистр I значения, отличные от 0 или 63. Tasword создавал особенные проблемы, так как в нем не работала комбинация Symbol Shift/A.

Причиной проблемы называли неоптимальную внутреннюю емкость клавиатуры, параметры которой «уплывают» по мере прогрева машины, влияя на тайминги сигналов. Это определенно объясняет температурный характер неисправности, который долгое время ставил меня в тупик.

Я заглянул внутрь своего Спектрума и увидел, что диод 35 на самом деле входит в цепочку из 8 диодов, идущих к клавиатуре.
